- When sentiment turns negative sharply (e.g., -1.00+), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After strong upward sentiment spikes (e.g., +2.00+), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to align with true mean reversion.
- High news volume (>3.0) correlates with over-forecasting; dampen forecast by 2–5% for high-news periods to account for noise.
- If sentiment change is +1.00 or higher, model often underestimates downward correction; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effect.
- When sentiment is flat (±0.33) and news is low, model tends to drift downward; apply upward bias of 1–3% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price in early cycles (first 5–7 days); add 1–3% to initial forecast to capture momentum bias.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often overreacts; reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overcorrection.
